$comment: never the script's internals, so there is exactly one place a ref name lives.
WHY THIS EXISTS — a real near-miss, 2026-09-10.
Promotion an internal ticket ('promote(dev->main)') was opened while `dev` was at one
tip. Two hours later an internal ticket merged DIRECTLY into `main`, so `main`
acquired 3 commits that `dev` did not have. an internal ticket sat open, still
describing itself as promoting N commits, with its base moved underneath
it. Nothing detected this. It was caught by hand, only because a full ref
census happened to compare origin/dev..origin/main in the non-obvious
THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE BUG. Everyone measures main..dev — how much is
waiting to promote. Almost nobody measures dev..main — what main gained
that dev lacks. The second is the dangerous one, and it reads zero in the
healthy case, so its absence from a dashboard is invisible. promotion-drift
measures the first direction; this gate measures the second.
$why_trunk: The integration trunk work is promoted FROM. It must FULLY CONTAIN the
target, or the promotion merges a base that has moved.
$why_target: The branch being promoted TO. Anything that lands here directly — a hotfix,
an admin merge, a revert — is exactly what this gate exists to catch,
because it is invisible to every count taken in the usual direction.
$why_no_threshold: This gate has no tunable number, deliberately. ONE commit on main that dev
lacks already means the promotion base has moved; there is no 'a little
stale is fine' regime to encode. The remedy is always the same and always
cheap: back-merge main into dev, then promote. A threshold here would only
be a place to hide the failure.
$why_first_parent: Counts are reported as INDEPENDENT LANDINGS (--first-parent) alongside raw
cost scales with the number of independent changes in a batch, not with how
many commits each carried. Measured on csq 2026-09-10: origin/main..
origin/dev was 13 raw but 9 first-parent — raw overstates by 1.44x.
$why_freshness_is_fatal: A remote-tracking ref only updates on fetch. A run against a STALE
origin/main reports GREEN while main has in fact moved — which is this
gate reproducing the exact bug it exists to catch. So the gate FETCHES
first, and a fetch it cannot complete is UNDETERMINED (exit 2), never a
pass. PBS_NO_FETCH=1 exists only for fixtures whose refs ARE ground truth;
it downgrades the freshness claim in the output rather than hiding it.
